To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 5′-noncoding region of prfA mRNA that contains the ribosome binding site and the first 20 amino acid codons is required for efficient ribosome loading.
a 5′-end of the prfAmRNA is essential for efficient translation.
the prfA coding region is required for efficient translational expression of the prfAMRNA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a thermoregulation expression system, which could be of use for other applications in biotechnology.
the identification of a novel translational expression system based on the thermoregulated prfA-mRNAs.
the development of a new thermoregulated expression system for the expression of heterologous genes in E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 5′-region of the prfAmRNA, which is not structured, is required for maximal expression of the mRNA.
the first 20-30 codons of the prf A-mRNA are essential for maximal expression.
the prfA-UTR and the first 20 amino acids of the prfACDS are both necessary for high expression levels of prfA and prfA-dependent genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prfA 5′-region is important for translation, and this is a prerequisite for PrfA-dependent gene regulation.
the 5′ coding region of the prfa-mRNA is required for efficient ribosome binding, and that a hairpin-loop immediately downstream of the ribosome binding site (RBS) is important for ribosome binding.
the 5′ UTR of the prf A mRNA is important to ensure efficient translation, and that the first 20 amino acid codons of the prf -mRNA are important for maximal expression.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prfA 5′-leader is not sufficient for translational control and that the first 20-30 codons are important for maximal expression.
the prfA coding sequence can be used to regulate the expression of heterologous genes in a thermosensitive manner in both E. coli and L. monocytogens.
the prfA-5′-UTRs are not just a thermoregulatory device but are also important for the translational regulation of the PrfA regulon in L. monocytognes.
